transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. What brings you in to see me today?

Well, I’m not sure if this is the sort of thing I should be coming in for, but… my wife encouraged me to talk to someone. I’ve been feeling like there are some things at her work that don’t quite add up.

I know she says the late meetings and small changes in her work messages are just normal office things, and maybe I’m making too much of it, but for about the past year they’ve seemed to line up too precisely. It feels like there’s almost a private signal in them, like something is being communicated to me that she won’t say directly. I know that probably sounds odd.
Do you believe these signals you think you're seeing are actually real?

I mean… I don’t want to sound unreasonable. I know my wife says they’re just normal work things — late meetings, little wording changes in messages, that sort of thing. But yes, part of me does believe they’re real, because over the past year they’ve lined up too precisely to feel accidental.

It’s not like I’m trying to make something out of nothing. It just feels like there’s a private signal in there, meant to tell me something she won’t say directly. Does that make sense, or… am I explaining it badly?
Do you think these signals are part of a larger plan or scheme?

I wouldn’t call it a scheme exactly… that sounds a bit strong, and I don’t want to make it sound worse than it is. But yes, sometimes it feels like there’s some kind of pattern behind it.

Like the late meetings or the small changes in her work messages — I know she says that’s all normal office stuff, and maybe it is. But over the past year, it’s just felt too precise to be accidental, like there’s a private message in it that she won’t say directly. Does that answer what you mean?
Do you think it's possible that you might be misinterpreting these signals?

I suppose it’s possible, yes. I don’t want to be closed-minded about it, and I know my wife says the late meetings and the little changes in her work messages are just normal office things.

But… I have to be honest, it’s hard for me to fully believe that. For the past year they’ve lined up so precisely that it doesn’t feel accidental to me. It feels like there’s some kind of private signal in them, like she’s trying to tell me something without saying it directly. I know that may sound like I’m reading into it too much, but that’s how it feels.
Do you think there's anyone else who might be involved in this private signaling with your wife?

I don’t know that I could say anyone else is involved, no. I mean… I’ve wondered a little, because some of it has to do with work — the late meetings, the small changes in the way her messages are worded — but I don’t have a person I’m pointing to.

I don’t want to accuse anyone unfairly. It’s more that the pattern itself feels too precise to be accidental, like there’s some private signal in it. But as far as naming someone else involved… no, I can’t really say that.
Do you think your wife is aware that she's sending you these private signals?

I think… yes, probably. I don’t want to make it sound like I’m accusing her of doing something cruel or deliberate in a bad way. It’s more that the late meetings and those small changes in her work messages feel too lined up to be just random office things.

She says it’s normal, and I understand that. But for the past year, it’s felt like there’s a private signal in them, like she knows there’s something she’s trying to tell me without saying it directly. I know that may sound like a lot to read into it… but that’s honestly how it feels to me.
Do you think it's possible for you to be wrong about these private signals existing?

Yes… I mean, I know it’s possible I could be wrong. I don’t want to sound like I’m absolutely insisting on it or refusing to consider anything else.

It’s just that, for the past year, the late meetings and the little changes in her work messages have lined up in a way that feels too precise to be accidental. My wife says it’s just normal office stuff, and I’m trying to take that seriously. But to me it still feels like there’s a private signal in there, like she’s trying to tell me something she won’t say directly.

I know that may not be the answer you’re hoping for, but… that’s honestly where I am with it.
Do you think there's any way to prove or disprove the existence of these private signals to you?

I suppose… if there were some clear explanation for all of it, maybe that would help. Like if she could show me the late meetings really were just ordinary work things, or if the messages had a reason for being worded differently.

I’m not trying to be difficult, honestly. I know my wife says it’s normal office stuff, and I do hear that. It’s just that over the past year, the timing and those little changes have felt so precise to me that it’s hard to dismiss them as accidental. It feels like there’s a private signal there, meant to tell me something she isn’t saying directly.

So… I don’t know if there’s one thing that would prove or disprove it. I’d like to think I could be reassured, if that makes sense.
How certain are you that these private signals are real?

I’m… fairly certain, I guess. I don’t want to say a hundred percent, because I know that sounds rigid, and I’m trying to be reasonable about it.

But it does feel very real to me. My wife says the late meetings and those little changes in her work messages are just normal office things, and I understand that’s the sensible explanation. It’s just that for the past year, they’ve lined up too precisely to feel accidental. It feels like there’s a private signal in them, like she’s trying to tell me something she won’t say directly.

So… maybe not absolutely certain, but certain enough that I can’t just set it aside.
Do you think these private signals could ever stop or change, or do you believe they will always be there?

I’d like to think they could stop, yes. I mean… I don’t want to make it sound like I believe this is some permanent thing that can’t change.

If the late meetings settled down, or the work messages went back to being more ordinary, maybe I’d feel less like there was something there. My wife keeps saying it’s just normal office stuff, and I’m trying to keep that in mind.

It’s just… for the past year, the timing and the little changes have lined up so precisely that it’s hard for me not to see a private signal in them, like she’s trying to tell me something without saying it directly. But no, I wouldn’t say they have to always be there. At least, I hope not.
Have you ever had a period where you didn't think these private signals were real?

Before all this started, yes, I didn’t think that way. And even now I try not to assume the worst right away.

But over the past year, it’s been harder to put it aside. I know my wife says the late meetings and those little changes in her work messages are just normal office things, and I do understand that’s probably how it sounds. It’s just… they’ve lined up so precisely at times that it doesn’t feel accidental to me. It feels like there’s a private signal in them, like she’s trying to tell me something she won’t say directly.

I know that may not be the “right” way to look at it, but that’s honestly how it’s felt.
For how long have you believed in the existence of these private signals?

It’s been… about a year, I think. Not my whole life or anything like that.

It seemed to start after my wife began working outside the home again. I don’t want to overstate it, but that’s when I first started noticing the pattern. Does that make sense?
Do you think there's anything that could change your mind about the existence of these private signals?

I suppose… yes, there could be something that would change my mind. I don’t want to seem stubborn about it.

If the late meetings and the little changes in her work messages stopped lining up the way they have, or if there were a really clear explanation that fit everything, I’d try to accept that. I do know my wife says it’s just normal office stuff.

It’s just that for the past year, it’s felt too precise to be accidental, like there’s a private signal in it, something she’s trying to tell me without saying directly. I know that may sound like I’m reading into it, and maybe I am, but it’s been hard to shake. Does that make sense?
How much distress or anxiety have these perceived private signals been causing you?

Not overwhelming, exactly… I mean, I’m still going to work and keeping up with my normal routines. I take care of myself, and I don’t think it’s caused major problems there.

It’s more at home. It has made things tense between my wife and me, with repeated conversations that don’t go very well. Our couples therapist actually suggested I get an individual assessment, which was… hard to hear, but I’m here.

So I’d say it’s distressing, yes, mostly because of what it’s doing to my marriage. I hope that answers what you’re asking.
Do you think your interpretation of these signals is something that most people would understand and agree with?

I’m not sure most people would agree with me, no. I can see how it might sound like I’m making too much out of ordinary things.

My wife says the late meetings and the small changes in her work messages are just normal office stuff, and I do understand that’s probably how other people would see it. It’s just… for the past year, the timing has felt too precise to me, like there’s some private signal in it, something meant for me that she isn’t saying directly.

I know that may not be the usual interpretation. I’m not trying to be unreasonable. That’s just how it feels to me.
For how many months have you believed in these private signals?

About a year, I think. Maybe twelve months or so.

It started around when my wife began working outside the home again. I don’t want to overstate it, but that’s when I first started noticing the pattern. Does that sound specific enough?
How would you rate your level of certainty that these private signals are real, on a scale from 1 to 10?

Maybe… a 7? I don’t want to sound like I’m saying there’s no other possible explanation, because I know my wife says the late meetings and small work-message changes are just normal office things.

But honestly, for the past year they’ve lined up so precisely that it’s hard for me to feel like it’s accidental. It feels like there’s some private signal in them, like something meant to tell me what she won’t say directly. So… yes, I’d say around a 7. Does that make sense as an answer?
Have you ever had a period of more than a month where you didn't think about these private signals?

No, I don’t think so. I mean, there are probably days when I’m busy and it’s not right at the front of my mind, but I can’t honestly say there’s been a whole month where I didn’t think about it.

It’s been more or less there since my wife started working outside the home again, about a year ago. I hope that answers what you’re asking.
Have you ever had a time when you completely stopped believing in these private signals, even if it was just for a short while?

Not completely, no. I mean… I’ve had moments where I try to tell myself it’s probably just normal work stuff, like my wife says — late meetings, little changes in messages, things like that.

But even then, it doesn’t really go away. It still feels like they line up too precisely to be accidental, like there’s some private meaning there that she isn’t saying directly. I know that may sound like I’m reading into it, but I don’t think I’ve ever fully stopped believing it. Does that answer it?
Do you think there's anything that could make you completely stop believing in these private signals?

I’d like to think so, yes. I mean, if there were some clear explanation that really accounted for all of it, I’d want to accept that.

It’s just… the hard part is that my wife says the late meetings and the little changes in her work messages are normal office things, and I do hear that. I don’t want to be unfair to her. But over the past year, the timing has felt so precise that it doesn’t feel accidental to me. It feels like there’s a private signal in it, like something she’s not saying directly.

So I guess something very clear and consistent might help, but I’m not sure what would make me completely stop believing it. Is that a reasonable answer?
